source.original_text: Attributed implementation component of Algorithm 3.1 with Appendix D.1/D.2 approximate proximal queries, not a convergence theorem. Under the normalized C2 Hessian bounds and 0<eta<=c<1, eps>0, construct one measurable stopped proximal map q, its exact proximal comparison p, and its successful gradient-test count N+1. For h>=0 and supplied finite deterministic node and quadrature arrays, draw independent zeta0,zeta1,G0,G1 from the product of two standard Gaussian laws and two finite products of standard Gaussian laws. Set a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)), P0=a P+sigma zeta0, Y0_i=X+t_i P0, Z0_j=grad V(q(Y0_j)+sqrt(eta)G0_j), Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j, Z1_j=grad V(q(Y1_j)+sqrt(eta)G1_j), Xnext=X+h P0-sum_j positionWeight_j Z1_j and Pnext=a(P0-sum_j momentumWeight_j Z1_j)+sigma zeta1. The joint update Phi is measurable and defines a Markov kernel K(s,.)=map(Phi(s,.),gamma); at every queried y the actual finite interpreter with fuel N(y)+1 returns (q(y),N(y)+1) and ||q(y)-p(y)||<=eps. Source node/weight construction and the repeated-run accuracy/cost theorems remain separate.

lean.statement:
For every E,iota with [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace R E] [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional R E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [Fintype iota],
{V : E → ℝ} {κ : ℝ≥0}
    (hκ : 1 ≤ κ) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E, (κ : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    {eta c eps : ℝ} (heta : 0 < eta) (hec : eta ≤ c) (hc : c < 1) (heps : 0 < eps)
    (h : ℝ) (hh : 0 ≤ h) (t : ι → ℝ) (omega : ι → ι → ℝ)
    (positionWeight momentumWeight : ι → ℝ) :
    ∃ p q : E → E, ∃ N : E → ℕ,
      Measurable p ∧ Measurable q ∧ Measurable N ∧
      (∀ y, p y + eta • gradient V (p y) = y ∧ ‖q y - p y‖ ≤ eps ∧
        run (gradient V) eta eps y (N y + 1) y =
          some (q y, N y + 1)) ∧
      let a := Real.exp (-h / 2)
      let sigma := Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))
      let γ := ((stdGaussian E).prod (stdGaussian E)).prod
        ((Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)).prod
          (Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)))
      let Φ := fun w : (E × E) × ((E × E) × ((ι → E) × (ι → E))) =>
        let P0 := a • w.1.2 + sigma • w.2.1.1
        let Y0 := fun i => w.1.1 + t i • P0
        let Z0 := fun j => gradient V (q (Y0 j) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.1 j)
        let Y1 := fun i => Y0 i - ∑ j, omega i j • Z0 j
        let Z1 := fun j => gradient V (q (Y1 j) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.2 j)
        (w.1.1 + h • P0 - ∑ j, positionWeight j • Z1 j,
          a • (P0 - ∑ j, momentumWeight j • Z1 j) + sigma • w.2.1.2)
      0 ≤ 1 - Real.exp (-h) ∧
      Measurable Φ ∧ ∃ K : Kernel (E × E) (E × E), IsMarkovKernel K ∧
        ∀ s, K s = γ.map (fun z => Φ (s, z))
decoder_context: The finite interpreter run(g,eta,eps,y,fuel,x) returns none at zero fuel; at positive fuel it evaluates g(x), sets next=y-eta*g(x), and returns some(x,1) if ||next-x||<=(1-eta)*eps. Otherwise it recurses at next with one less fuel and adds one to a successful returned query count. All arithmetic is exact real arithmetic.

stdGaussian E is the centered Gaussian probability measure with identity covariance. Measure.pi is the finite product of the indicated probability measures; prod is the product measure. map is measurable pushforward.
A Markov kernel K has a probability measure K(s) at each incoming state s, with measurable dependence on s for every measurable output event. All finite sums range over the entire finite index type.
gradient is the real inner-product gradient, fderiv the real Frechet derivative, and smul scalar multiplication. Arrays t,omega,positionWeight,momentumWeight are deterministic real-valued functions.

reconstruction.text:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its Borel measurable structure, and let I be any finite index type. Let V:E->R be C^2 and let kappa be a nonnegative real with 1<=kappa. Suppose that, for every x,v in E,
  kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
Fix real eta,c,epsilon such that 0<eta<=c<1 and epsilon>0, a real h>=0, and arbitrary deterministic arrays t:I->R, omega:I x I->R, b:I->R, and d:I->R. Here b and d denote positionWeight and momentumWeight.
Then there exist measurable maps p,q:E->E and N:E->N such that for every y in E,
  p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y,
  ||q(y)-p(y)||<=epsilon,
  run(grad V,eta,epsilon,y,N(y)+1,y)=some(q(y),N(y)+1).
The finite exact-real interpreter run(g,eta,epsilon,y,fuel,x) fails with none when fuel is zero. With positive fuel it sets next=y-eta g(x). If ||next-x||<=(1-eta)epsilon it returns (x,1); otherwise it recurses from next with one less unit of fuel and adds one to the successful query count. Thus the displayed equality supplies a finite successful run starting at y, using fuel N(y)+1, with output q(y) and reported count exactly N(y)+1.
For these witnesses put a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)), and let gamma be the product law of mutually independent standard Gaussian E-valued variables u,v,(xi_j)_{j in I},(xi'_j)_{j in I}; explicitly gamma=(G x G) x ((product_I G) x (product_I G)), where G is the centered Gaussian probability measure with identity covariance. For an incoming state s=(x,r) in E x E and a noise sample z=((u,v),(xi,xi')), define
  P0=a r+sigma u,
  Y0_i=x+t_i P0,
  Z0_j=grad V(q(Y0_j)+sqrt(eta) xi_j),
  Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_{j in I} omega_{ij} Z0_j,
  Z1_j=grad V(q(Y1_j)+sqrt(eta) xi'_j),
  Phi(s,z)=(x+h P0-sum_{j in I} b_j Z1_j,
            a(P0-sum_{j in I} d_j Z1_j)+sigma v).
Then 1-exp(-h)>=0, Phi is jointly measurable on (E x E) x ((E x E) x ((I->E) x (I->E))), and there exists a Markov kernel K from E x E to E x E satisfying, for every s,
  K(s)=(z -> Phi(s,z))_* gamma.
Equivalently, for every Borel output event A, K(s,A)=gamma({z:Phi(s,z) in A}); each K(s) is a probability measure and its value on each measurable event depends measurably on s. All sums use the entire finite index type. This statement asserts the existence and measurability of these witnesses and transition kernel; it gives no invariant-distribution, convergence, bias, or uniform query-complexity conclusion.

domains.original: The pinned component accepts a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, a finite deterministic index set, nonnegative h and arbitrary finite real node/weight arrays. The source algorithm itself uses Euclidean phase space, J>=2 and its Chebyshev-Lobatto arrays.
domains.reconstructed: Complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel E; any finite index type I; h>=0; t,omega,b,d arbitrary deterministic real arrays.

quantifiers.original: For fixed normalized C2 V, eta,c,eps and supplied arrays, construct common measurable witnesses p,q,N valid at every queried center and a kernel valid at every incoming state.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every admissible space,potential,parameters and arrays, there exist p,q,N with forall y execution/accuracy certificates, followed by an existential K with forall s exact law.
quantifiers.evidence: The phase theorem obtains p,N and defines q before constructing Phi. Both layers use the identical q. The certificates hold for all y, including random centers; the driving law is a constant kernel independent of the incoming state. No realization-dependent existential oracle replaces the common measurable map.

assumptions.original: C2 normalized Hessian bounds kappa^(-1)I<=Hessian V<=I with kappa>=1, 0<eta<=c<1, eps>0, h>=0; finite supplied arrays.
assumptions.reconstructed: The same quadratic-form Hessian inequalities at every x,v; the same parameter inequalities and finite-array conditions.
assumptions.evidence: The source normalization is in Section 3 and Algorithm D.2 assumes precisely 0<eta<=c0<1. Positivity eps>0 is needed for finite stopping; D.1 allows zero accuracy abstractly but D.2 does not. No D.1 stability step-size restriction or repeated-run parameter choice is needed for this kernel existence component, and none is assumed or claimed.

conclusion.original: A measurable stopped query with eps accuracy and successful finite interpreter count, and a jointly measurable explicit update whose independent Gaussian pushforward is a Markov transition law.
conclusion.reconstructed: Measurable p,q,N; exact proximal optimality equation, eps norm error and run success with N+1 fuel/count; nonnegative refresh variance, measurable Phi and Markov K with K(s)=Phi(s,.)_*gamma.
conclusion.evidence: The parent establishes that p is the unique minimizer of V(x)+(2 eta)^(-1)||x-y||^2, so the phase optimality equation legitimately identifies the exact proximal comparison. The probability-kernel statement is a Samplinglib measure-theoretic elaboration, expressly attributed as such; it does not assert a source convergence theorem. The decoder event-law reformulation follows from measurable pushforward.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ApproximateProximalExecution
import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Multivariate
import Mathlib.Probability.Kernel.Composition.Prod
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.Pi

/-!
# The implemented two-layer Picard phase

Chen--Chewi--Lu--Zhang, arXiv:2609.06906v1, Algorithm 3.1 steps 1--4,
with the gradient-only proximal implementation of Appendix D.1/D.2.
The kernel below uses both independent Gaussian arrays and both half-refreshes.
Every proximal evaluation is the actual finite residual-stopped program.

Finite deterministic nodes and quadrature weights are inputs of this bounded
interface. Their Chebyshev--Lobatto construction, repeated-history estimates,
sampling error, invariant law, and expected run cost remain separate.
-/

noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory InnerProductSpace
open scoped BigOperators NNReal

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ImplementedPhaseKernel

variable {E ι : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
  [Fintype ι]

/-- The full two-layer phase is a measurable Markov kernel, with its law given
by the explicit independent Gaussian pushforward and every proximal draw bound
to the actual stopped interpreter. No quadrature or convergence premise is
assumed to manufacture a kernel. -/
theorem implemented_phase_kernel {V : E → ℝ} {κ : ℝ≥0}
    (hκ : 1 ≤ κ) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E, (κ : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ ‖v‖ ^ 2)
    {eta c eps : ℝ} (heta : 0 < eta) (hec : eta ≤ c) (hc : c < 1) (heps : 0 < eps)
    (h : ℝ) (hh : 0 ≤ h) (t : ι → ℝ) (omega : ι → ι → ℝ)
    (positionWeight momentumWeight : ι → ℝ) :
    ∃ p q : E → E, ∃ N : E → ℕ,
      Measurable p ∧ Measurable q ∧ Measurable N ∧
      (∀ y, p y + eta • gradient V (p y) = y ∧ ‖q y - p y‖ ≤ eps ∧
        ApproximateProximalExecution.proximalQuery (gradient V) eta eps y (N y + 1) y =
          some (q y, N y + 1)) ∧
      let a := Real.exp (-h / 2)
      let sigma := Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h))
      let γ := ((stdGaussian E).prod (stdGaussian E)).prod
        ((Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)).prod
          (Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)))
      let Φ := fun w : (E × E) × ((E × E) × ((ι → E) × (ι → E))) =>
        let P0 := a • w.1.2 + sigma • w.2.1.1
        let Y0 := fun i => w.1.1 + t i • P0
        let Z0 := fun j => gradient V (q (Y0 j) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.1 j)
        let Y1 := fun i => Y0 i - ∑ j, omega i j • Z0 j
        let Z1 := fun j => gradient V (q (Y1 j) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.2 j)
        (w.1.1 + h • P0 - ∑ j, positionWeight j • Z1 j,
          a • (P0 - ∑ j, momentumWeight j • Z1 j) + sigma • w.2.1.2)
      0 ≤ 1 - Real.exp (-h) ∧
      Measurable Φ ∧ ∃ K : Kernel (E × E) (E × E), IsMarkovKernel K ∧
        ∀ s, K s = γ.map (fun z => Φ (s, z)) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨p, N, hp, hN, hq, hall⟩ :=
    ApproximateProximalExecution.approximate_proximal_execution
      hκ hV hH heta hec hc heps
  let q := fun y => (fun x : E => y - eta • gradient V x)^[N y] y
  have hqm : Measurable q := hq
  refine ⟨p, q, N, hp, hqm, hN, fun y =>
    ⟨(hall y).1, (hall y).2.2.2.2.1, (hall y).2.2.2.2.2.2⟩, ?_⟩
  dsimp only
  have hg : Measurable (gradient V) := by
    unfold gradient
    exact ((InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E).symm.continuous.comp
      (hV.continuous_fderiv (by norm_num))).measurable
  let γ := ((stdGaussian E).prod (stdGaussian E)).prod
    ((Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)).prod
      (Measure.pi (fun _ : ι => stdGaussian E)))
  let Φ := fun w : (E × E) × ((E × E) × ((ι → E) × (ι → E))) =>
    let P0 := Real.exp (-h / 2) • w.1.2 + Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h)) • w.2.1.1
    let Y0 := fun i => w.1.1 + t i • P0
    let Z0 := fun j => gradient V (q (Y0 j) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.1 j)
    let Y1 := fun i => Y0 i - ∑ j, omega i j • Z0 j
    let Z1 := fun j => gradient V (q (Y1 j) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.2 j)
    (w.1.1 + h • P0 - ∑ j, positionWeight j • Z1 j,
      Real.exp (-h / 2) • (P0 - ∑ j, momentumWeight j • Z1 j) +
        Real.sqrt (1 - Real.exp (-h)) • w.2.1.2)
  have hΦ : Measurable Φ := by
    dsimp only [Φ]
    fun_prop
  let K := (Kernel.id ×ₖ Kernel.const (E × E) γ).map Φ
  have hK : IsMarkovKernel K := Kernel.IsMarkovKernel.map _ hΦ
  refine ⟨sub_nonneg.mpr (Real.exp_le_one_iff.mpr (by linarith)),
    hΦ, K, hK, fun s => ?_⟩
  dsimp only [K]
  rw [Kernel.map_apply _ hΦ, Kernel.prod_apply, Kernel.id_apply, Kernel.const_apply,
    Measure.dirac_prod, Measure.map_map hΦ (by fun_prop)]
  rfl

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ImplementedPhaseKernel

steps.lean: approximate_proximal_execution supplies p,N and the measurable stopped iterate; hall supplies its certificate.

steps.title: Keep all Gaussian draws independent
steps.text: The two refresh coordinates have independent standard Gaussian laws. Two additional finite product factors supply independently fresh arrays G0 and G1, independent also of the incoming state in the kernel product. Product mass one follows from Mathlib probability instances.
steps.lean: stdGaussian, Measure.prod and Measure.pi construct the explicit law gamma.

steps.title: Construct the first refreshed trajectory and layer
steps.text: h>=0 makes the refresh variance nonnegative. Coordinate projections, finite sums, scalar multiplication and addition are measurable. C2 regularity makes grad V continuous, so the stopped q and each stochastic-gradient evaluation preserve measurability.
steps.formula: P_0=aP+\sigma\zeta_0,\quad Y_i^0=X+t_iP_0,\quad Z_j^0=\nabla V(q(Y_j^0)+\sqrt\eta G_j^0),\quad Y_i^1=Y_i^0-\sum_j\omega_{ij}Z_j^0.
steps.lean: The gradient is the continuous dual isometry applied to fderiv; hqm, hg and fun_prop certify the entire joint update.

steps.title: Use the second fresh array and complete the phase
steps.text: The second gradient array evaluates q at the first updated centers, using G1 rather than reusing G0. Separate terminal position and momentum weights produce the second Picard outputs. The final refresh uses zeta1. No node or weight error estimate is assumed in this construction.
steps.formula: Z_j^1=\nabla V(q(Y_j^1)+\sqrt\eta G_j^1),\quad X^+=X+hP_0-\sum_j b_jZ_j^1,\quad P^+=a(P_0-\sum_j m_jZ_j^1)+\sigma\zeta_1.
steps.lean: The explicit lets Z1 and the output pair retain both final sums and the second refresh in Phi.

steps.title: Construct the canonical Markov kernel
steps.text: Combine the identity kernel at the incoming state with the constant probability kernel gamma, and map it by the jointly measurable Phi. At s this product is delta_s tensor gamma. The Dirac-product and composition-of-map identities give the stated pushforward exactly.
steps.lean: Kernel.IsMarkovKernel.map proves mass one; Kernel.map_apply, Kernel.prod_apply, Measure.dirac_prod and Measure.map_map prove the exact output law.

lesson.lean_statement: The exact statement displays the independent Gaussian law and complete update map under lets; every proximal call shares the actual certified stopped map.
lesson.lean_proof: Construct the stopped map once, prove the explicit update jointly measurable, and map the canonical product Markov kernel.

candidate_assumptions.source: The normalized C2 Hessian bounds and Algorithm D.2 parameter range.
candidate_assumptions.lean: V is C2, kappa >= 1 and kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D2V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2 for every x,v. 0 < eta <= c < 1, eps > 0 and h >= 0.

candidate_assumptions.source: Algorithm 3.1 uses source Chebyshev–Lobatto nodes and integral weights.
candidate_assumptions.lean: t, omega, positionWeight and momentumWeight are supplied finite real arrays. Their source quadrature definitions and bounds are not conclusions of this interface.

candidate_assumptions.source: Independent standard Gaussian variables in Algorithm 3.1.
candidate_assumptions.lean: Two standard Gaussian factors and two finite independent Gaussian-array factors, followed by an explicit joint measurable update.

candidate_assumptions.source: A Euclidean state space with J>=2 nodes and positive phase length.
candidate_assumptions.lean: An arbitrary complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, finite index type and nonnegative h.
